key_insight: DeepRubric improves reinforcement learning for deep research agents by generating query–rubric supervision from evidence trees, so the reward criteria match the true information needs of a report.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more sample-efficient way to train research agents with rubric-based RL, achieving competitive benchmark results with far fewer GPU-hours.
method: Start from a seed topic and recursively expand it into an evidence tree of sub-questions.
Use the tree’s leaf nodes as atomic, verifiable evaluation targets.
Synthesize aligned query–rubric pairs so the reward checks exactly what the query asks for.
evidence_signal: The authors built 9K query–rubric supervision examples and reported comparable performance to prior open state of the art across three benchmarks with about 13x fewer RL GPU-hours.
watch_item: The approach depends on the quality of the evidence tree and rubric synthesis, so weak decomposition or incomplete evidence could still lead to misaligned supervision.
paper_title: DEEPRUBRIC: Evidence-Tree Rubric Supervision for Efficient Reinforcement Learning of Deep Research Agents
